sender.en: A new client, employer or buyer, often a “parent moving from overseas”

name.en: Fake check: “I sent too much, please send back the difference”

how.en: Someone hires you or buys from you, for example a parent who says they are moving to your area from overseas and needs childcare right away. They send a check for more than the agreed amount, then say it was a mistake and ask you to send back the extra by wire transfer, a payment app, gift cards or crypto. The check may seem to clear and the money shows in your account, but days later it bounces and you must repay the bank.

text.en: A new client contacts you and needs your service urgently, often from overseas.
They send a check for more than the agreed price.
They say it was a mistake and ask you to send back the difference by wire, payment app or gift cards.
The check bounces and the bank takes the money back from you.

Hi! We are relocating to your area from London next week and need a nanny for our two kids right away. I will mail you a check in advance. My assistant sent it for $2,450 instead of $450 by mistake, please send the extra back by Zelle today.

en: A check for more than the agreed amount.
A request to send back the difference by wire, payment app, gift cards or crypto.
A new client who is urgent, abroad, or never meets you.
Being paid before you have done any work.
Don’t accept a check for more than you charge.
Never send money back to someone who says they overpaid you by check.
Money showing in your account doesn’t mean the check is good. Ask your bank and wait.
If you sent money, contact the company you used right away.
